summary: Edge healthcheck traffic + subaccount failover reprofiles causing intermittent 429s on mixed-priority routes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported repeated 429 responses across several API routes after they performed a subaccount failover and we rolled a configuration tweak to edge caching earlier that morning. The 429s are intermittent but correlate with short waves (1-3m) of elevated healthcheck and scheduling traffic. Impact: production embedding and chat calls returned 429s for multiple API keys during the waves, causing stalled ingestion and user-visible errors.

Impact:
- BrightCart reported 15-40% of requests returned 429 during two 2–5 minute waves between 2026-03-12T09:14:00Z and 2026-03-12T09:22:00Z.
- Customer sla: Dedicated pool with predictability requirement; user-facing search index backfills stalled.

Environment:
- prod-us-west primary, failover to eu-west for some subaccounts.
- Dedicated pool: d-pool-34 (GPU-backed).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Simulate a subaccount failover (reparenting jobs) while running scheduled background flushes + healthcheck probes to origin-edge.
2) Observe elevated 429s on mixed-priority routes (chat and embed endpoints).

Observed behaviour:
- 429 responses with standard throttle headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining occasionally omitted).
- Throttles appear to snap on then off in waves; correlated with healthcheck bursts and reweighted route priorities.

Expected behaviour:
- Healthchecks and internal scheduling probes should be accounted separately or routed to isolated burst pools so customer interactive routes are not starved.

Additional data provided by customer:
- Sample request-ids: rq_8f7a2b3c, rq_8f7a2b6d during first wave.
- Approx timestamps: 2026-03-12T09:15:08Z, 2026-03-12T09:19:57Z.
- They attached an abbreviated client-side retry log (supplied on initial ticket).

Request:
- Please investigate why healthcheck and subaccount failover correlated with tenant-level 429s and provide mitigation / config guidance to avoid recurrence.
comments: 2026-03-12 | Aisha Khan: Opened ticket after customer provided logs and retry traces. Noted correlation with our edge cache tweak rolled at 2026-03-12T08:47Z and BrightCart's subaccount failover at ~09:12Z.
2026-03-12 | Marco Reyes (SRE): Acknowledged; kick off triage. Asked customer for full request headers and whether healthchecks are coming from fixed IPs. Added SRE on-call. (Assigned: Marco Reyes)

2026-03-12 | BrightCart Support (customer): Provided healthcheck CIDR 198.51.100.0/24 and confirmation they performed reparent at 09:11Z. Noted that healthchecks are standard TCP/HTTP probes once every 10s per instance.
They also confirmed background flush interval is 30s for ingestion workers.

2026-03-12 | Marco Reyes (SRE): Initial triage - found token-debit spikes on tenant bucket around the timestamps. Noted duplicate accounting on proxied preflight and cache-miss paths. Captured Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd/rate-accounting?panelId=4&from=1678676100000&to=1678676520000

2026-03-13 | Marco Reyes (SRE): Applied temporary exemption for provided healthcheck CIDR (edge.healthcheck_exempt) to prevent probes from charging tenant burst credits while we investigate. Monitoring for recurrence. Asked ENG to review rate-limiter dedupe logic for proxied path normalization.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 10:00Z - Correlation observed: momentary spike in ingress connections from healthcheck CIDR simultaneously with subaccount reparent operations.

Edge proxy change rolled at 2026-03-12T08:47Z introduced a path normalization rewrite for signed-url callbacks that caused some requests to be counted twice at the token-accounting layer (preflight + origin).

Subaccount failover temporarily reweighted route priority weights; background flush jobs increased concurrent requests to the dedicated pool and consumed burst tokens faster than normal smoothing logic could compensate.
Rate-limiter logs show sequence: accept -> preflight -> forward -> accounting increment twice when path rewrite toggles 'X-Orig-Path'.
Evidence: rate-limiter trace ids rl_00423 and rl_00424 (see attached logs in customer upload). Prometheus counters rate_limiter_debits{tenant="brightcart"} spiked by ~3.5x during windows.
root_cause: A conjunction of: (1) edge path rewrite after edge cache tweak caused duplicate accounting of certain proxied preflight/signed-url requests, and (2) a temporary change in route weights from a subaccount failover caused background flush traffic to consume burst credits faster than smoothing windows adjusted—this led to tenant-level burst exhaustion and transient 429s.
resolution: Mitigation executed: temporarily exempted BrightCart's healthcheck CIDR from tenant burst accounting and reverted the path-normalization rule for signed-url callbacks in the edge-proxy config. Engineering PRs created for permanent fixes (rate-limiter dedupe + path-normalization gating).
resolution_notes: Temporary: edge.healthcheck_exempt configured for 198.51.100.0/24 at 2026-03-12T17:20Z (no further 429 waves observed after exemption window).
Rollback: edge-proxy path normalization rollback deployed to canary at 2026-03-12T19:40Z (ticketed in PR https://github.com/redwood/edge-proxy/pull/782).

Permanent fix: rate-limiter change to dedupe accounting for preflight/forward pairs when X-Connection-ID and normalized path match. PR: https://github.com/redwood/rate-limiter/pull/410 (code review in progress, schedule for 2026-03-20 rollout).

Customer guidance: recommend isolating healthchecks into separate route (route weight 0 and burst pool exemption) or configuring a dedicated low-priority burst pool for background flushes. Provided configuration playbook snippet to customer.
follow_up_actions: INT-2041: Add unit & integration tests for accounting dedupe (assigned to backend team)
Schedule a postmortem with BrightCart and internal SRE/ENG to review rollout checklist for edge changes (owner: Marco Reyes)
Update public docs/console guidance on 'separating healthchecks and background workers' and provide example configs for dedicated customers
customer_communication: 2026-03-12 | Support: Notified BrightCart that we're investigating and have requested headers and CIDRs.
2026-03-13 | Support: Confirmed temporary exemption applied and suggested customer set healthchecks to a dedicated route; requested that customer keep us updated if they see recurrence.
2026-03-13 | BrightCart: Confirmed that 429 waves stopped after exemption and rollback; asked for timeline for permanent fix.
public_notes: If you see similar behavior after edge config changes and failovers: check for healthcheck IP fanout and whether edge path rewrites could produce duplicate accounting. Consider isolating probes to an exempted CIDR or separate route/burst pool until dedupe fix is deployed.
